conditions.exact_rule_quote: the tenant has, on or after the 9th day of June, 1952, sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises
conditions.description: The tenant sub-let, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or any part of the premises.
conditions.scope: Section 14(1)(b) conduct element for the fixed Delhi eviction ground.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952
conditions.description: The relevant subletting, assignment, or parting with possession occurred on or after 9 June 1952.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
conditions.description: The relevant subletting, assignment, or parting with possession occurred without the landlord's written consent.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: the onus to prove sub-letting is on the landlord
conditions.description: The landlord bears the onus to prove subletting.
conditions.scope: Supplied Supreme Court authority passage addressing the burden for a Delhi DRC section 14 subletting ground.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: If the landlord prima-facie shows that the occupant who was in exclusive possession of the premises let out for valuable consideration, it would then be for the tenant to rebut the evidence.
conditions.description: A prima-facie showing of an occupant in exclusive possession for valuable consideration shifts the evidentiary burden to the tenant to rebut.
conditions.scope: Supplied burden-shifting mechanism; the source itself cautions that mere presence is not equivalent to exclusive possession for consideration.

bindings.stage: Addl. Rent Controller merits decision, 29 August 1974
bindings.reason: The preserved trial-level finding directly states that the petitioner had sublet the premises; it is supporting input evidence only and is not treated as target-court adoption.

bindings.stage: Rent Control Tribunal rehearing after remand
bindings.reason: The Tribunal on rehearing upheld the earlier finding that the premises had been sublet; this supports the conduct proposition while remaining a lower-court finding.
The tenant's preserved challenge contests the correctness of the lower-court subletting finding. As a CLAIMED proposition it tends against c1 but does not establish that subletting was false.

The tenant claimed that no positive finding of consideration had been recorded. That claim tends against treating the frozen input as expressly satisfying the valuable-consideration component of the supplied prima-facie trigger, without establishing that consideration was absent.
